stimuli.title: Case study: fall in long-term care
stimuli.text:
Long-term care facility, night shift. An 84-year-old resident with Parkinson disease, atrial fibrillation, osteoporosis and mild dementia is found on the floor.

History: Parkinson disease for 8 years. Atrial fibrillation. Osteoporosis. Mild dementia. No known drug allergies. Weight 62 kg. Code status: full code. Baseline on the care plan: walks with a walker and standby assistance, oriented to person and place, and uses the call light inconsistently.

At 0240 the assistive personnel (AP) calls the PN. The resident is sitting on the floor beside the bed and says, "I needed the bathroom and didn't want to bother anyone."

Medications
- carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg PO three times daily
- apixaban 5 mg PO twice daily
- alendronate 70 mg PO weekly
- donepezil 5 mg PO at bedtime
- zolpidem 5 mg PO at bedtime, started 3 nights ago

| 0245 data collection | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 104/62 mm Hg sitting (afternoon reading 132/78) |
| Heart rate | 92/min, irregular |
| Respirations | 18/min |
| Temperature | 97.8 F |
| Pain | Right hip 2 of 10; no shortening or rotation of the leg |
| Head | Small bump above the left ear, skin intact; speech clear, no facial droop |
| Orientation | Person and place, same as baseline |
| Room | Bed in the low position, call light on the floor, floor dry, resident barefoot |

stimuli.title: Case study: hypoglycemia in a long-term care resident
stimuli.text:
Long-term care facility, 1130. A 79-year-old resident with type 2 diabetes for 20 years, hypertension and mild chronic kidney disease. Weight 61 kg. No known allergies.

Baseline, per the assistive personnel (AP) who care for her every day: alert, oriented to person and place, chats during care, and walks to the dining room with a walker. Usual blood pressure is in the 130s/80s. She eats in the dining room and takes her morning medicines there.

The AP reports that the resident ate about 25% of breakfast at 0800, saying her stomach was upset, and that the 0800 medicines were given. At 1130 the AP finds her in her room, says she "does not seem like herself," and calls the PN. A bedside glucose has not been checked yet.

Medications
- glipizide 10 mg PO before breakfast
- insulin glargine 20 units subcut at bedtime (last dose 2100 yesterday)
- lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
- atorvastatin 20 mg PO at bedtime

| 1130 data | Finding |
|---|---|
| BP | 138/82 mm Hg |
| Heart rate | 104/min |
| Respirations | 20/min |
| Temperature | 97.9 F |
| SpO2 | 96% on room air |
| Skin | Cool and sweaty |
| Breakfast | About 25% eaten; glipizide given at 0800 |

stimuli.title: Case study: depression at a diabetes clinic visit
stimuli.text:
Outpatient diabetes clinic, 1000. A 58-year-old client with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and obesity comes in for a 3-month follow-up. The client's spouse died 5 months ago. The client lives alone and has stopped attending the weekly diabetes support group.

Medications: metformin 1,000 mg PO twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg PO daily, atorvastatin 20 mg PO at bedtime. No known allergies. The chart does not yet record whether today's doses were taken.

The client says, "I don't see the point in checking my sugar anymore."

| Clinic data | Today | 3 months ago |
|---|---|---|
| Weight | 88 kg | 95 kg |
| BP | 148/88 mm Hg | 134/82 mm Hg |
| A1C | 9.4% | 7.6% |
| Glucose log | 6 entries in 3 months | 2 entries daily |
| Sleep | "4 hours, up at 3 a.m. most nights" | 7 hours |
| PHQ-2 score | 5 of 6 | 1 of 6 |
| Support | Lives alone; left the diabetes group after the death | Attended the group weekly |

questions.stem: The RN is making assignments on a medical-surgical unit. Which client is the most appropriate for the RN to assign to the PN?
options: Stable client with COPD taking oral antibiotics
Newly admitted client with chest pain awaiting evaluation
Client whose blood transfusion started 10 minutes ago
Client with new confusion the morning after surgery
questions.explanation: The PN cares for clients whose condition is stable and predictable, such as a client with COPD who is improving on oral antibiotics. A new admission with chest pain, the first 15 minutes of a transfusion and new postoperative confusion all need the RN's assessment and judgment.

questions.stem: Metoprolol tartrate 75 mg PO is prescribed. The pharmacy supplies 25 mg tablets. How many tablets should the PN give? Record your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: 75 mg divided by 25 mg per tablet is 3 tablets. Setting up the problem as 25 divided by 75 gives 0.33 tablet, which cannot be measured and would be one third of the prescribed dose.

questions.passage: 0800 Nurses' note, postoperative day 1 after an open bowel resection: {{Temperature 101.6 F}}. {{Incision edges together with slight pink redness along the line}}. {{Right calf tender and swollen compared with the left}}. {{Bowel sounds hypoactive in all four quadrants}}. {{Pain 3 of 10 after the morning dose of oxycodone}}. {{Urine output 25 mL/hr for the last 2 hours}}. {{Crackles heard in both lung bases}}.
questions.stem: The PN collects data on the client. Highlight the findings that should be reported to the RN.
questions.explanation: A fever of 101.6 F, a tender swollen calf (possible deep vein thrombosis), urine output below 30 mL/hr and crackles in the bases (atelectasis or fluid) are all complications that need the RN and provider. Hypoactive bowel sounds, slight incisional redness and well-controlled pain are expected the day after bowel surgery.

questions.stem: The PN is preparing to give medications to a resident who has dementia and cannot state her name. How should the PN identify the resident?
options: Check the wristband against the medication record
Ask the roommate to confirm the resident's full name
Use the photo on the door as the only check
Ask the resident to nod when her name is said
questions.explanation: Two identifiers from the wristband, such as name and date of birth, are checked against the medication record every time. A roommate, a door photo alone or a nod from a confused resident are not reliable identifiers.

questions.stem: A client who has just learned of a cancer diagnosis says to the PN, "Why did this happen to me?" Which response is therapeutic?
options: "This must be very hard to take in."
"Everything happens for a reason."
"The doctors here are the best."
"Try not to think about it right now."
questions.explanation: Reflecting the client's feelings invites the client to keep talking. Cliches, false reassurance and telling the client not to think about it all shut the conversation down.

questions.stem: The PN observes a client with weakness in the left leg walking with a standard walker. Which observation shows correct technique?
options: Moves the walker, then steps in with the weaker leg
Lifts the walker off the floor to turn around in the hall
Leans the trunk forward over the walker while walking
Steps the stronger leg forward before moving the walker
questions.explanation: The walker is moved forward first, then the weaker leg steps into it so the arms share that leg's load, and the stronger leg follows. Leaning over the walker or leading with the strong leg leaves the weak leg unsupported, and the walker should stay on the floor while turning in small steps.

questions.stem: The PN collects data on a long-term care resident with stable COPD. For each finding, specify whether it is expected for this resident or should be reported to the RN.
questions.explanation: A resting saturation around 88% to 92%, a barrel chest and pursed-lip breathing are the long-term picture of COPD. New confusion and drowsiness suggest carbon dioxide retention or low oxygen, and fever with green sputum suggests a respiratory infection, both of which need the RN and provider.

questions.stem: A client at 10 weeks of pregnancy asks the PN which foods to avoid. Which food should the PN say to avoid?
options: Unpasteurized soft cheese
Cooked salmon twice a week
Pasteurized yogurt
Peanut butter on toast
questions.explanation: Unpasteurized dairy can carry Listeria, which crosses the placenta and can cause miscarriage or stillbirth. Low-mercury cooked fish, pasteurized dairy and peanut butter are safe and nutritious in pregnancy.

questions.stem: The PN is assigning tasks to assistive personnel (AP) on a long-term care unit. Which task is appropriate to assign to the AP?
options: Reinforce teaching about a new inhaler
Walk a stable resident in the hallway
Check a new skin tear and describe it
Give a scheduled oral medication
questions.explanation: Walking a stable resident is a routine task with a predictable outcome that AP can perform. Reinforcing teaching, collecting data on a new skin tear and giving medications require nursing knowledge and stay with the PN.

questions.stem: Amoxicillin 400 mg PO is prescribed. The oral suspension is labeled 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the PN give? Record your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: 250 mg per 5 mL is 50 mg per mL, and 400 mg divided by 50 mg/mL is 8 mL. Reading the label as 250 mg per mL would give 1.6 mL, less than half the dose.

questions.stem: A client's morning potassium level is 2.9 mEq/L. Which finding should the PN watch for and report?
options: Muscle weakness and an irregular pulse
Tall, peaked T waves on the monitor
Twitching around the mouth
Watery diarrhea and cramping
questions.explanation: Low potassium weakens skeletal muscle and makes the heart irritable, so weakness, leg cramps and an irregular pulse are the signs to report. Peaked T waves go with high potassium, and twitching around the mouth suggests low calcium.

questions.stem: The PN is caring for a client 1 day after abdominal surgery. Which finding should the PN report to the RN immediately?
options: Pain 4 of 10 after an oral analgesic
Bowel sounds absent in all four quadrants
Dressing saturated with bright red blood
Urine output of 60 mL over the past hour
questions.explanation: A dressing saturated with bright red blood signals active bleeding and must be reported at once. Absent bowel sounds on the first day after abdominal surgery, mild pain after an analgesic and an output of 60 mL/hr are expected findings.

questions.stem: A provider prescribes a soft wrist restraint for a confused client who keeps pulling at a nasogastric tube. Which action by the PN is correct?
options: Tie it to the movable side rail with a square knot
Tie it to the bed frame with a quick-release knot
Remove it only when the family is visiting
Keep it on for 48 hours before the order is renewed
questions.explanation: A restraint is tied to a part of the bed frame that moves with the client, using a knot that staff can release in one pull. A side rail can trap the limb when it is lowered, the restraint is released and the skin checked at regular intervals per policy, and orders are renewed at least every 24 hours.

questions.stem: A resident whose spouse died 1 month ago cries during care and says, "I keep expecting him to call." How should the PN interpret this?
options: A sign of complicated grief
An expected grief response
A symptom of major depression
The start of dementia
questions.explanation: Crying, yearning and momentarily expecting the person to still be there are normal in the first months after a loss. Grief is considered complicated when intense symptoms persist for a year or more or stop the person from functioning.

questions.stem: While bathing a client, the PN finds a shallow open area over the coccyx with a pink-red, moist wound bed and no slough or bruising. Which stage should the PN report to the RN?
options: Stage 1
Stage 2
Stage 3
Unstageable
questions.explanation: A shallow open wound with a pink-red bed and no slough is a stage 2 pressure injury (partial-thickness skin loss). Stage 1 skin is intact, stage 3 shows fat in the wound bed, and unstageable means slough or eschar hides the base.

questions.stem: A client with diabetes becomes sweaty, shaky and anxious an hour before lunch. Which problem should the PN suspect?
options: Hyperglycemia
Hypoglycemia
Diabetic ketoacidosis
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
questions.explanation: Sweating, tremor, anxiety and hunger are the adrenergic signs of low blood sugar and come on quickly before a meal. High glucose states develop over hours to days with thirst, frequent urination and dry skin.

questions.stem: The PN is reinforcing teaching with the parents of a 2-day-old newborn. Which statement shows the teaching was effective?
options: "We'll put a small pillow in the crib for comfort."
"We'll place the baby on the back to sleep."
"We'll keep the bedroom at 80 degrees."
"We'll give water between feedings."
questions.explanation: Back sleeping on a firm, bare surface is the main way to lower the risk of sudden infant death. Pillows and soft bedding, an overheated room and water feedings in a newborn are all unsafe.

questions.stem: A competent adult client refuses the scheduled morning dose of warfarin. What should the PN do?
options: Ask the family to persuade the client
Mix the crushed tablet into applesauce
Hold the dose and chart it as given
Document the refusal and notify the RN
questions.explanation: A competent adult has the right to refuse any medication, so the PN documents the refusal and tells the RN, who informs the provider. Hiding a medication in food or charting a held dose as given is deceptive and falsifies the record.

questions.passage: 0900 Laboratory result: INR 4.8 (goal 2.0 to 3.0). The PN notes new bruising on both forearms. Warfarin 5 mg PO is due at 1700.
questions.stem: Complete the sentence. The PN should [[1]] and report the result to the [[2]].
blanks: give a double dose of warfarin
give the dose with vitamin K-rich food
oncoming shift at the end of the day
pharmacy at the end of the shift
questions.explanation: An INR of 4.8 with new bruising means the blood is too thin and bleeding has started, so the dose is held and the RN or provider is told now, not at shift change, because they may prescribe vitamin K. Vitamin K foods would lower the INR unpredictably and are not how a high INR is managed.

questions.stem: A client scheduled for surgery at 0800 tells the PN at 0700, "I had a piece of toast an hour ago." Which action should the PN take?
options: Document the intake and send the client to surgery
Notify the RN right away
Give an antacid and continue the preoperative checklist
Reschedule the surgery for the afternoon
questions.explanation: Food within the fasting window raises the risk of aspiration during anesthesia, so the RN and surgical team must know before the client leaves the unit; they decide whether to delay. The PN reports the data and does not reschedule surgery or cover the problem with an antacid.

questions.stem: The PN is caring for a client with Clostridioides difficile diarrhea. Which action is most important for preventing transmission?
options: Use alcohol-based hand rub after care
Wear an N95 respirator in the room
Wash hands with soap and water after care
Place the client in a negative-pressure room
questions.explanation: C. difficile spores are not killed by alcohol, so hands are washed with soap and water to remove them, along with contact precautions and bleach cleaning. The infection spreads by contact, not through the air, so respirators and negative pressure are not needed.

questions.stem: A resident with dementia becomes agitated every evening and insists on "going home to make dinner." Which approach should the PN use?
options: Remind the resident that this is her home now
Explain that her house was sold years ago
Offer a simple task such as folding towels
Ask the resident why she wants to leave
questions.explanation: Redirecting to a familiar, purposeful activity calms a resident with dementia without arguing about facts she cannot retain. Reality orientation and explanations about the sold house increase distress, and asking why requires reasoning the resident no longer has.

questions.stem: A client is 1 day after a total hip replacement through a posterior approach. Which position should the PN maintain?
options: Hips flexed past 90 degrees for comfort
Operative leg crossed over the other leg
Legs separated with an abduction pillow
Lying on the operative side
questions.explanation: After a posterior approach, the legs are kept abducted with a wedge pillow and the hip is not flexed beyond 90 degrees, crossed or turned inward, because those positions can dislocate the new joint. Lying on the operative side is avoided in the early days.

questions.stem: In a crowded elevator, a coworker asks the PN about the diagnosis of a well-known client on the unit. Which response is appropriate?
options: "I can't discuss any client here."
"Only if you promise not to repeat it."
"It has already been in the news."
"Ask the charge nurse after the shift."
questions.explanation: Client information is shared only with staff who need it for care and never in a public place. A promise of secrecy or the diagnosis being in the news does not remove the client's right to privacy.

questions.stem: A client begins a tonic-clonic seizure in bed. Which action should the PN take?
options: Place a padded tongue blade between the teeth to protect the tongue
Hold the arms and legs still until the movements stop
Turn the client onto the side and protect the head
Leave the room to get the RN and the emergency cart
questions.explanation: Side-lying lets saliva drain and keeps the airway open, and padding protects the head while the seizure runs its course. Nothing goes in the mouth, limbs are never restrained because that causes injury, and the PN stays with the client and calls for help.

questions.stem: Before giving digoxin to an adult client, the PN counts an apical pulse of 54/min for one full minute. Which action should the PN take?
options: Hold the dose and notify the RN
Give the dose and recheck the pulse in 1 hour
Give half the dose and document the pulse
Give the dose with a full glass of water
questions.explanation: Digoxin slows the heart, so a dose is held and reported when the apical pulse is below 60/min in an adult. Giving any part of the dose at this rate risks a dangerous bradycardia, and the PN does not change a prescribed dose.

questions.stem: A resident with a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order chokes during lunch and is coughing forcefully. What should the PN do?
options: Perform abdominal thrusts immediately
Stay with the resident and encourage coughing
Take no action because of the DNR order
Call the provider to confirm the DNR order
questions.explanation: A DNR order applies only to resuscitation after cardiac or respiratory arrest; the resident still receives every other treatment, including help with choking. A forceful cough means air is moving, so the PN encourages coughing and intervenes with abdominal thrusts only if the airway becomes blocked.

questions.stem: A client is 1 day after abdominal surgery. Which measures should the PN use to prevent atelectasis and pneumonia? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage 10 breaths an hour on the incentive spirometer while awake
Keep the client flat in bed to rest the incision
Help the client splint the incision with a pillow while coughing
Help the client walk in the hall as prescribed
Hold the pain medication so the client stays alert
questions.explanation: Deep breathing with the spirometer, coughing with the incision supported and early walking re-expand the lungs. Lying flat and uncontrolled pain both keep breaths shallow, which is what causes atelectasis.

questions.stem: A parent asks the PN whether a 12-month-old's development is on track. Which milestone is expected at 12 months?
options: Walks up stairs alternating feet
Builds a tower of six blocks
Pulls to a stand
Speaks in two-word sentences
questions.explanation: By 12 months most infants pull to stand, cruise along furniture and say one or two words. Alternating feet on stairs and six-block towers come around age 3, and two-word sentences around age 2.

questions.stem: The PN discovers a small fire in a trash can in an empty client room. The PN moves nearby clients away and pulls the alarm. Which action is next?
options: Turn off the oxygen to the whole unit
Call the fire department from the room
Use the extinguisher on the fire
Close the doors to confine the fire
questions.explanation: RACE is Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish, so after rescue and the alarm the PN closes doors to contain the smoke and fire, then extinguishes a small fire if it is safe. Oxygen shutoff is done by the person designated in the facility plan, usually the charge nurse.

questions.stem: At a clinic, the PN notices bruises in different stages of healing on a 6-year-old's back. The parent says the child "falls a lot." What should the PN do?
options: Ask the parent to explain each bruise
Accept the explanation and document it
Confront the parent about abuse
Report suspected abuse per state law
questions.explanation: Nurses are mandated reporters, so suspected child abuse is reported to the RN and provider and to the child protective agency according to state law; proof is not required. Confronting the parent can put the child at greater risk, and accepting an explanation that does not fit the injuries fails the child.

questions.stem: A long-term care resident taking scheduled oxycodone for arthritis pain has not had a bowel movement in 3 days. Which actions should the PN take? Select all that apply.
options: Offer fluids throughout the day
Encourage walking in the hall
Hold the oxycodone until a bowel movement
Give the prescribed stool softener
Give a soap suds enema every day
questions.explanation: Opioid constipation is managed with fluids, activity, fiber and the prescribed bowel regimen, usually a stool softener with a stimulant laxative. Holding pain medication causes needless pain, and daily enemas irritate the bowel and are not a prevention plan.

questions.stem: A client asks the PN what a durable power of attorney for health care does. Which explanation is correct?
options: Lists the treatments you refuse at the end of life
Gives your lawyer control of your finances
Names someone to make care decisions if you can't
Takes effect only after a terminal diagnosis
questions.explanation: A durable power of attorney for health care names a person to make health decisions when the client can no longer make them. A living will is the document that lists treatment wishes, and neither document deals with finances.

questions.stem: A client received regular insulin subcutaneously at 0730 before breakfast. At which time should the PN watch most closely for hypoglycemia?
questions.explanation: Regular insulin starts working in about 30 minutes and peaks 2 to 3 hours after the dose, so the highest hypoglycemia risk is mid-morning. 0745 is before the onset, and 1600 or 2200 fit an intermediate-acting insulin such as NPH.

questions.stem: The PN collects data on a client with heart failure. Which findings suggest the condition is getting worse and should be reported? Select all that apply.
options: Weight gain of 3 lb in 2 days
Needs two pillows to breathe at night
Ankle swelling that is increasing
Urine output increased after the diuretic
Heart rate 72/min and regular
questions.explanation: Rapid weight gain, needing to sleep propped up and growing edema all mean fluid is building up. Good urine output after a diuretic and a normal regular pulse show the treatment is working.

questions.stem: A clinic client is scheduled for a colonoscopy. Which statement shows the client understands the reinforced preparation instructions?
options: "I can eat a light breakfast the morning of the test."
"I'll stop the bowel prep once I have diarrhea."
"I'll have only clear liquids the day before."
"Red gelatin is a good clear liquid to choose."
questions.explanation: A clear liquid diet the day before and the full bowel preparation are what let the provider see the colon wall. Diarrhea means the prep is working and it is finished as directed, nothing is eaten the morning of the test, and red or purple liquids are avoided because they look like blood.

questions.stem: The PN is giving a handoff report at the end of the shift. Which information is most important to include?
options: The client walked in the hall twice
The client's family asked about visiting hours
The client prefers the window blinds closed
A pending potassium level for a digoxin client
questions.explanation: A pending lab result that can change care, such as a potassium level in a client taking digoxin, must be handed off so the next nurse follows it up. Routine activity and preferences are documented but are not safety-critical.

questions.passage: 0250 AP note: Found resident sitting on the floor at 0240 beside the bed. {{Call light on the floor}}. {{Bed in the low position}}. {{Resident barefoot}}. {{Says the new sleeping pill made her "woozy"}}. {{Floor dry}}. {{Small bump above the left ear}}. {{Oriented to person and place}}. {{BP 104/62 sitting; 132/78 this afternoon}}.
questions.stem: The PN reviews the AP's note and the data collected. Highlight the findings that require follow-up.
questions.explanation: A call light out of reach, bare feet, sedation from a new sleep aid, a head strike in a resident taking an anticoagulant and a 28-point drop in systolic pressure all need action or reporting. A low bed, a dry floor and orientation at baseline are expected and need no follow-up.

questions.stem: The PN analyzes the resident's history. For each factor, specify whether it raises the risk of falling, raises the risk of injury from a fall, or does neither.
columns: Raises the risk of injury from a fall
questions.explanation: Parkinson disease, a new sedative and dementia all make a fall more likely through unsteady gait, drowsiness and poor judgment about calling for help. Apixaban and osteoporosis do not cause falls but make bleeding and fractures more likely when one happens; alendronate treats the osteoporosis and does neither.

questions.passage: 0300: Orthostatic vital signs: lying BP 128/76 mm Hg, HR 88/min; standing BP 100/60 mm Hg, HR 98/min. The resident reports dizziness on standing.
questions.stem: Complete the sentence. The resident's fall was most likely caused by [[1]], and the resident is now at greatest risk for [[2]].
blanks: a pressure injury on the hip
questions.explanation: A 28 mm Hg drop in systolic pressure on standing with dizziness, in a resident with Parkinson disease who started a sedative 3 nights ago, explains the fall. Hitting the head while taking apixaban makes intracranial bleeding the greatest danger, which is why neurologic checks are ordered.

questions.passage: 0300: The RN has evaluated the resident and notified the provider. New orders: neurologic checks every hour for 4 hours, then every 4 hours for 24 hours; hold zolpidem; orthostatic vital signs; right hip x-ray in the morning; fall precautions.
questions.stem: The PN is planning care for the rest of the night. Which tasks can the PN assign to the AP? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the bed low with the call light in reach
Perform the hourly neurologic checks
Check on the resident every hour during rounding
Decide whether the hip x-ray is still needed
Help the resident to the bathroom with the walker
Report any vomiting or increased sleepiness at once
questions.explanation: The AP can keep the room safe, round hourly, assist with walking and report what they observe. Neurologic checks require nursing judgment, so the PN performs them and reports changes to the RN, and the x-ray decision belongs to the provider.

questions.passage: 0315: The resident is drowsier than at 0245, vomited once and now answers only to name. Right pupil 3 mm, left pupil 5 mm, both react slowly.
questions.stem: Which action should the PN take first?
options: Notify the RN immediately
Give the scheduled carbidopa-levodopa early
Apply a cold pack to the bump on the head
Repeat the neurologic check in 15 minutes
questions.explanation: New drowsiness, vomiting and unequal pupils after a head strike in a resident taking apixaban point to bleeding inside the skull, so the PN reports to the RN at once so emergency transfer can be arranged. Waiting 15 minutes to recheck delays treatment, and a cold pack does nothing for intracranial bleeding.

questions.passage: Two weeks later. The CT scan at the hospital showed no bleeding and the resident returned the next day. Zolpidem was stopped and the resident joined an afternoon exercise group. The AP reports the resident "used the call light every night this week" and walked to the bathroom with the walker. The resident says, "I'm scared of falling in the dining room, so I eat in my room."
questions.stem: The PN evaluates the resident's progress. Which findings show that the plan of care is working? Select all that apply.
options: Uses the call light before getting up at night
Walks to the bathroom with the walker and standby assistance
Eats meals alone in the room
Has had no further falls
Attends the exercise group
Avoids the dining room out of fear
questions.explanation: Calling for help, walking safely with the walker, no new falls and joining the exercise group are the goals of the fall plan being met. Eating alone because of fear of falling is social withdrawal that the PN reports to the RN so the plan can address the fear.

questions.stem: The PN is giving a subcutaneous injection. Which action prevents a needlestick injury?
options: Activate the safety shield right after the injection
Recap the needle with two hands before disposal
Set the used syringe on the tray to discard later
Bend the needle before placing it in the sharps box
questions.explanation: The safety device is activated immediately and the syringe goes straight into a sharps container at the point of use. Two-handed recapping, carrying an uncovered needle and bending needles are the actions that cause needlesticks.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old client at average risk asks the PN at what age colorectal cancer screening should start. Which response is accurate?
options: "At age 40."
"At age 50."
"At age 60."
"At age 45."
questions.explanation: Current guidelines recommend that adults at average risk begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45. Earlier screening is for people with a family history or other risk factors, and 50 was the former starting age.

questions.stem: A client scheduled for surgery in an hour is pacing, has trembling hands and says, "I can't stop thinking about it." Which action should the PN take first?
options: Stay with the client and speak calmly
Ask the client to describe the surgery
Give the preoperative sedative early
Leave the client alone to calm down
questions.explanation: A calm presence lowers anxiety and lets the PN find out what the client is worried about. Asking for details of the surgery can increase fear, medications are given as prescribed, and leaving an anxious client alone increases distress.

questions.skill: Oral care for an unconscious client
questions.stem: The PN provides mouth care to an unconscious client. Which action is correct?
options: Rinse the mouth with a large amount of water and let it drain
Sit the client straight up at 90 degrees for the procedure
Use lemon and glycerin swabs to moisten the dry mucosa
Turn the client to the side with the head turned toward the PN
questions.explanation: A side-lying position with the head turned lets fluid drain out of the mouth instead of into the airway, and only small amounts of fluid are used with suction nearby. Lemon-glycerin swabs dry and irritate the mucosa, and an unconscious client cannot be safely propped straight up for oral care.

questions.stem: The PN prepares to give oral medications on a medical unit. Which actions are part of safe administration? Select all that apply.
options: Check two client identifiers at the bedside
Leave the cup at the bedside for the client to take later
Compare the MAR with the medication label three times
Crush an enteric-coated tablet to make it easier to swallow
Stay until the client has swallowed the medications
questions.explanation: Two identifiers, three label checks and watching the client swallow are the core of the rights of medication administration. Medications are never left unattended, and crushing an enteric-coated tablet destroys the coating that protects the stomach or the drug.

questions.stem: The PN sees a coworker take a client's oral opioid from the medication cart and put it in a pocket. What should the PN do?
options: Report the observation to the supervisor
Confront the coworker privately first
Wait to see whether it happens again
Ask the client whether the dose was given
questions.explanation: Suspected drug diversion is reported to the supervisor right away so the client is protected and the facility can investigate. Confronting the coworker or waiting for a second event delays protection of the client and can allow evidence to disappear.

questions.stem: A client takes warfarin after a deep vein thrombosis. Which laboratory value should the PN check before giving the dose?
options: aPTT
Platelet count
Hemoglobin
INR
questions.explanation: Warfarin is monitored with the INR (goal usually 2.0 to 3.0). The aPTT monitors heparin, and platelets and hemoglobin do not show how much the blood is thinned.

questions.stem: A long-term care resident suddenly has drooping on one side of the face and slurred speech. Which action should the PN take first?
options: Give aspirin 325 mg from the stock supply
Offer a sip of water to test swallowing
Help the resident walk back to bed
Note the time and alert the RN immediately
questions.explanation: A stroke is treated against the clock, so the time the symptoms were last normal is recorded and the RN activates emergency care at once. Nothing is given by mouth until swallowing is cleared, aspirin is unsafe if the stroke is a bleed, and walking risks a fall.

questions.stem: A clinic client is starting a 10-day course of an oral antibiotic for a skin infection. Which statement shows the reinforced teaching was effective?
options: "I'll stop as soon as the redness is gone."
"I'll save any leftover pills for the next time."
"I'll finish the whole prescription."
"I'll take two pills if I miss a dose."
questions.explanation: Finishing the full course clears the infection and limits resistant bacteria. Stopping early, saving pills or doubling up all lead to treatment failure or side effects.

questions.stem: A provider calls the unit with a new prescription for a high-alert IV medication. The PN answers the phone. Per facility policy and state scope, PNs on the unit do not take telephone orders for high-alert medications. What should the PN do?
options: Write the order and read it back
Transfer the call to the RN
Ask the provider to call back later
Enter the order for the RN to co-sign
questions.explanation: When policy and state scope exclude the PN from taking the order, the PN hands the call to the RN, who takes and reads back the prescription. Writing or entering the order, even for a co-signature, is practicing outside the allowed role.

questions.stem: The PN wore gloves, a gown and a surgical mask to care for a client on contact and droplet precautions. Place the steps for removing the equipment in the order the PN should perform them.
options: Remove the gloves
Remove the gown
Leave the room and perform hand hygiene
Remove the mask by its ties or loops
Perform hand hygiene again
questions.explanation: Gloves are the most contaminated item and come off first, then the gown, and the mask is removed last, outside the room, touching only the ties, with hand hygiene after the gown and again after the mask. Removing the mask before the gloves brings contaminated gloves to the face.

questions.stem: A client with a new colostomy refuses to look at the stoma and says, "There's nothing wrong with me. The surgery was a mistake." The PN recognizes this as which coping mechanism?
options: Projection
Denial
Regression
Rationalization
questions.explanation: Refusing to accept that the illness and surgery were real is denial, a common early response to a change in body image. Projection blames others for one's own feelings, regression is a return to earlier behavior, and rationalization invents acceptable reasons.

questions.stem: The PN gives an intermittent bolus feeding through an established gastrostomy tube. Place the steps in the order the PN should perform them.
options: Raise the head of the bed to at least 30 degrees
Check tube placement and residual per facility policy
Flush the tube with 30 mL of water
Pour the formula into the syringe and let it flow by gravity
Flush the tube with water after the formula
Keep the head of the bed raised for 30 to 60 minutes
questions.explanation: The head is raised before anything goes in to reduce aspiration risk, placement and residual are checked per policy, the tube is flushed, the formula runs in by gravity, the tube is flushed again to keep it open, and the client stays upright afterward. Flushing after the feeding and leaving the head up are what keep the tube patent and the stomach contents down.

questions.stem: The PN is collecting data on a 78-year-old resident. Which finding is an expected change of aging?
options: Decreased sense of thirst
New confusion in the evening
Loss of bladder control
Resting tremor in one hand
questions.explanation: Thirst sensation declines with age, which is why older adults are at risk for dehydration and need fluids offered regularly. Confusion, incontinence and a resting tremor are signs of illness, not normal aging, and are reported to the RN.

questions.stem: The PN changes a dressing on a surgical incision that is 4 days old. Which findings should the PN report to the RN as possible infection? Select all that apply.
options: Thick yellow drainage from the incision
Warmth and redness spreading away from the incision
Pink, slightly raised edges along the incision
Temperature 101.2 F
Scant pink drainage on the old dressing
questions.explanation: Purulent drainage, spreading redness and warmth, and fever are the signs of wound infection. Pink raised edges and a small amount of serosanguineous drainage are part of normal healing.

questions.stem: A client scheduled for a colonoscopy tells the PN, "I signed the form, but I don't know what they're going to do." What should the PN do?
options: Explain the risks of the procedure to the client
Reassure the client that the form is signed
Notify the RN before the procedure
Ask the family to explain the procedure
questions.explanation: A signed form is not valid consent if the client does not understand the procedure, so the PN tells the RN, who contacts the provider to explain it again. Explaining risks and benefits is the provider's responsibility, not the nurse's or the family's.

questions.stem: A client is receiving oral oxycodone after surgery. Which finding should the PN report to the RN immediately?
options: Reports mild constipation
Pupils are small
Drowsy but wakes easily to voice
Respirations 8/min
questions.explanation: A respiratory rate of 8/min is opioid-induced respiratory depression and calls for holding the drug, stimulating the client and having naloxone given. Small pupils, mild drowsiness and constipation are expected opioid effects that are managed, not emergencies.

questions.stem: A client receiving IV fluids develops crackles in both lungs, shortness of breath and a bounding pulse. Which action should the PN take?
options: Raise the head of the bed and call the RN
Increase the IV rate to support the blood pressure
Lay the client flat to rest
Encourage the client to drink more fluids
questions.explanation: Crackles, dyspnea and a bounding pulse during an infusion mean fluid overload, so the client is sat up to ease breathing and the RN is called to slow the fluid and contact the provider. More fluid or lying flat makes it worse.

questions.stem: The PN has four residents to see at the start of the shift. Which resident should the PN see first?
options: Resident asking for a sleeping pill
Resident due for a dressing change
Resident whose glucose was 142 mg/dL
Resident with new slurred speech
questions.explanation: New slurred speech can be a stroke, which is time-critical, so the PN collects data and reports to the RN at once. A sleep aid, a routine dressing change and a glucose of 142 mg/dL can wait.

questions.stem: The PN is caring for a client on airborne precautions for suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Wear a fit-tested N95 respirator in the room
Keep the room door closed
Place a surgical mask on the client during transport
Use a negative-pressure room
Remove the N95 before leaving the room
Limit visits to 15 minutes without a respirator
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis spreads by tiny droplet nuclei that stay in the air, so staff wear a fit-tested N95, the door stays closed on a negative-pressure room, and the client wears a surgical mask when outside the room. The respirator is removed after leaving the room, and no one enters without one.

questions.stem: A hospitalized client from a culture different from the PN's does not make eye contact during teaching. How should the PN interpret this?
options: A lack of interest in the teaching
Confirmation that the client is depressed
A possible sign of respect
A sign that the client does not understand
questions.explanation: In many cultures avoiding direct eye contact with a caregiver is a sign of respect, so the PN continues the teaching and checks understanding by asking the client to repeat it. Reading the behavior as disinterest, depression or confusion assumes the PN's own cultural norms.

questions.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease is on a potassium-restricted diet. Which lunch choice shows the client understands the reinforced teaching?
options: Apple slices and white rice
Baked potato with the skin on
Orange juice and a sliced banana
Tomato soup with cooked spinach
questions.explanation: Apples and white rice are low in potassium. Potatoes with skin, oranges, bananas, tomatoes and spinach are all high-potassium foods that a client with kidney disease must limit.

questions.stem: A client returned 1 hour ago from a cardiac catheterization through the right femoral artery. Which finding should the PN report to the RN immediately?
options: The right foot is cool and pale
A quarter-sized bruise at the puncture site
Pedal pulses equal on both feet
The client reports the urge to void
questions.explanation: A cool, pale foot on the side of the puncture means blood flow to the leg is blocked by a clot or spasm and is an emergency. A small bruise, equal pulses and a full bladder are expected after the procedure and the fluids given with it.

questions.stem: A client takes phenytoin for a seizure disorder. Which instruction should the PN reinforce?
options: Brush and floss the teeth carefully every day
Take the medication only on days a seizure occurs
Stop the medication if drowsiness develops
Avoid all dairy products
questions.explanation: Phenytoin causes gum overgrowth, so careful daily oral hygiene and regular dental visits are reinforced. It is taken every day to keep a steady blood level, and stopping it suddenly can trigger seizures.

questions.stem: Which tasks can the PN assign to assistive personnel (AP) on a long-term care unit? Select all that apply.
options: Help a resident with a shower
Record how much of a meal a resident ate
Reinforce teaching about a low-sodium diet
Empty a urinary drainage bag and record the output
Collect data on a resident's new rash
Turn and reposition a resident every 2 hours
questions.explanation: Hygiene, measuring intake and output and repositioning are routine tasks AP perform for stable residents. Reinforcing teaching and collecting data on a new finding require nursing knowledge and stay with the PN, who reports the rash to the RN.

questions.stem: The PN is reinforcing teaching about breastfeeding with a new mother. Which points should the PN include? Select all that apply.
options: Feed the newborn 8 to 12 times in 24 hours
Expect at least 6 wet diapers a day after the first week
Give formula after each feeding to be sure the baby is full
Bring the baby to the breast with the mouth wide open
Limit each feeding to 5 minutes per breast
Refrigerated breast milk is good for up to 4 days
questions.explanation: Frequent feeding, six or more wet diapers, a wide-open latch and safe milk storage are the basics of successful breastfeeding. Routine formula top-ups reduce the milk supply, and feedings are not timed; the baby decides when to finish.

questions.stem: The PN collects data on a client with hyperthyroidism. Which findings should the PN expect?
options: Weight gain, cold intolerance and a slow pulse
Weight loss, heat intolerance and a rapid pulse
Weight gain, heat intolerance and a slow pulse
Weight loss, cold intolerance and a slow pulse
questions.explanation: Excess thyroid hormone speeds up metabolism, so the client loses weight, feels hot, sweats and has a fast pulse. Weight gain, cold intolerance and a slow pulse are the opposite picture of hypothyroidism.

questions.stem: Which actions by the PN reduce the risk of falls for a long-term care resident? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the bed in the lowest position
Raise all four side rails at night
Make sure the resident wears non-skid footwear
Answer call lights promptly
Keep the walker by the far wall so the floor is clear
Orient the resident to the room and the call light
questions.explanation: A low bed, non-skid footwear, quick answers to the call light and orientation to the room all lower fall risk. Four raised side rails are a restraint that residents climb over, and a walker out of reach makes the resident walk without it.

questions.passage: Medical unit, day 2, 0800. A 54-year-old client admitted 36 hours ago for cellulitis of the leg is sweating, tremulous and anxious and says, "I feel like bugs are crawling on me." BP 162/98 mm Hg, HR 118/min, temperature 100.2 F, lungs clear. The client reports drinking "six or seven beers a night" at home and had the last drink the evening before admission.
questions.stem: Complete the diagram by choosing 2 actions the PN should take, the condition the client is most likely experiencing, and 2 parameters the PN should monitor.

groups.label: Actions to take
options: Notify the RN immediately
Implement seizure precautions
Give the client black coffee
Turn off the lights and close the door
Apply wrist restraints

groups.label: Condition most likely experiencing
options: Alcohol withdrawal
Sepsis from the cellulitis
Panic attack
Hypoglycemia

groups.label: Parameters to monitor
options: Orientation and hallucinations
Blood pressure and heart rate
Urine output
Serum sodium

questions.explanation: Tremor, sweating, tachycardia, hypertension and tactile hallucinations 36 hours after the last drink in a heavy drinker are alcohol withdrawal, which can progress to seizures and delirium tremens, so the PN reports to the RN at once and sets up seizure precautions. Sepsis is less likely with a low-grade fever and clear lungs and would not cause tremor and crawling sensations; a dark, closed room and restraints worsen agitation and hallucinations.

questions.stem: A newly admitted long-term care resident tells the PN, "I just can't fall asleep here." Which action should the PN take first?
options: Request a prescription for a sleeping pill from the provider
Ask about the resident's bedtime routine at home
Encourage a long nap after lunch to make up the lost sleep
Serve the evening meal right before bed so she is full
questions.explanation: The PN collects data first: learning the resident's usual routine (bedtime, snack, lighting, prayer, reading) lets the team recreate it, which is the safest sleep aid for an older adult. Sedatives raise fall risk, daytime naps and a late heavy meal make nighttime sleep worse.

questions.stem: The PN is reviewing resident rights with a newly admitted long-term care resident. Which rights should the PN include? Select all that apply.
options: Refuse a prescribed treatment
Be free from restraints used for staff convenience
Review their own medical record
Choose which staff member gives their care
Have another resident's diagnosis explained on request
Have personal mail opened only by the resident
questions.explanation: Residents may refuse treatment, cannot be restrained for convenience, may see their own record and have their mail kept private. They cannot pick individual staff members or learn another resident's private health information.

questions.stem: The RN started a blood transfusion 30 minutes ago and, per facility policy and state scope, asked the PN to help monitor the client. The client now reports chills and low back pain. Which action should the PN take first?
options: Slow the rate and continue to observe
Stop the transfusion and call the RN
Give the prescribed acetaminophen and continue
Document the complaint and recheck in 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Chills and low back pain during a transfusion are classic signs of a hemolytic reaction, so the blood is stopped at once, the line is kept open with normal saline per policy, and the RN takes over. Slowing the rate or treating the symptoms lets more incompatible blood run in. The RN stays with the client for the first 15 minutes, when reactions are most likely; the PN helps monitor afterward only where policy and state scope allow.

questions.stem: A client with heart failure takes lisinopril and spironolactone. Which points should the PN reinforce? Select all that apply.
options: Avoid salt substitutes that contain potassium
Report a dry cough that does not go away
Rise slowly from sitting or lying
Take an over-the-counter potassium supplement daily
Seek emergency care for swelling of the lips or tongue
questions.explanation: Both drugs raise potassium, so potassium-containing salt substitutes and supplements are avoided; lisinopril can also cause a dry cough, dizziness on standing and angioedema, which is an emergency. A daily potassium supplement with these two drugs could cause dangerous hyperkalemia.

questions.stem: The PN finds a client on the bathroom floor. The client is alert and reports no pain. Which actions should the PN take? Select all that apply.
options: Collect vital signs and check for injury
Notify the RN
Complete an incident report per facility policy
Chart that an incident report was filed
Describe the fall objectively in the client's record
Tell the family that a staff member was at fault
questions.explanation: After a fall the PN collects data, notifies the RN, documents what was found in objective terms and completes an incident report. The report is a quality tool that is not mentioned in the client's record, and blame is never assigned to the family or in the chart.

questions.stem: The PN at a clinic is reinforcing lifestyle teaching with a 45-year-old client who has prediabetes. Which recommendations are correct? Select all that apply.
options: At least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week
Losing 5 to 7 percent of body weight
Replacing sugary drinks with water
Cutting out all carbohydrates
Checking blood glucose four times a day
Quitting tobacco use
questions.explanation: Moderate weight loss, regular activity, fewer sugary drinks and stopping tobacco are the proven ways to delay type 2 diabetes. Carbohydrates are reduced and chosen well, not eliminated, and prediabetes does not need glucose checks four times a day.

questions.stem: A clinic client was stung by a bee 10 minutes ago. Which findings indicate anaphylaxis and require emergency care? Select all that apply.
options: Wheezing with each breath
Swelling of the lips and tongue
Hives spreading over the chest and arms
Redness the size of a quarter at the sting
BP 80/50 mm Hg
questions.explanation: Airway swelling, wheezing, widespread hives and a falling blood pressure are a whole-body allergic reaction that needs epinephrine and emergency care now. Redness limited to the sting site is a local reaction.

questions.stem: The PN is preparing to give a client's oral medications. Which actions follow the rights of medication administration? Select all that apply.
options: Check the label against the medication record three times
Use two identifiers before giving the dose
Give a medication that a coworker prepared
Document the dose before it is given
Check the allergy band before a new antibiotic
Stay with the client until the medications are swallowed
questions.explanation: Three label checks, two identifiers, an allergy check and staying until the dose is taken are the safeguards of safe administration. A nurse gives only medications they prepared and documents only after the dose is taken.

questions.stem: A client with a history of depression tells the PN, "I've been giving away my things, and I feel calm now." Which actions should the PN take? Select all that apply.
options: Ask the client directly about thoughts of suicide
Notify the RN immediately
Stay with the client
Promise to keep the conversation private
Remove items that could be used for self-harm per policy
Tell the client that things will look better tomorrow
questions.explanation: Giving away possessions and sudden calm can mean a decision to die, so the PN asks directly, stays with the client, secures the environment and gets the RN. Promising secrecy is unsafe and cannot be kept, and false reassurance dismisses what the client said.

questions.stem: A client with chronic low back pain asks the PN about using a heating pad at home. Which instruction should the PN reinforce?
options: Place the heating pad directly on bare skin
Use the highest setting for faster relief
Leave the heat on all night while sleeping
Limit each application to about 20 minutes
questions.explanation: Heat is applied over a cloth layer on a low to medium setting for about 20 minutes at a time; longer or hotter applications cause burns and rebound vasoconstriction. Falling asleep on a heating pad is a common cause of burns in older adults.

questions.stem: A client with a new forearm cast reports pain that is getting worse despite the prescribed analgesic, with numbness and tingling in the fingers. Which problem should the PN suspect and report?
options: Normal discomfort as the cast dries
Fat embolism
Compartment syndrome
Osteomyelitis
questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion that medication does not relieve, with numbness and tingling, is compartment syndrome from pressure inside the cast and needs the RN and provider at once. Fat embolism causes breathing changes and confusion, and osteomyelitis develops over days with fever.

questions.stem: A client who takes metformin is scheduled for a CT scan with IV contrast. Which instruction should the PN reinforce?
options: Take an extra dose the morning of the scan
Hold the metformin as directed around the scan
Take it with the contrast to prevent nausea
Stop the metformin permanently after the scan
questions.explanation: Iodinated contrast can reduce kidney function for a few days, and metformin builds up in that setting and can cause lactic acidosis, so the provider directs when to hold it and when to restart after kidney function is checked. It is resumed, not stopped for good, once the kidneys are shown to be fine.

questions.stem: The PN is reinforcing discharge teaching with a client who had a hip replacement. Which actions are within the PN's role? Select all that apply.
options: Review the written instructions the RN prepared
Create the discharge teaching plan
Answer questions about using the walker as taught
Report to the RN that the client cannot describe the medication schedule
Decide the client no longer needs home health
Demonstrate the hip precautions again
questions.explanation: The PN reinforces teaching the RN has planned, repeats demonstrations, answers questions within the plan and reports gaps in the client's understanding. Creating the teaching plan and changing the discharge plan are RN and provider decisions.

questions.stem: The PN's shift assignment includes a client receiving a continuous IV heparin infusion whose rate is adjusted from lab results. Per facility policy and state scope, PNs do not titrate IV infusions. What should the PN do?
options: Accept the client and change the rate only when the RN is busy
Tell the charge RN before accepting the assignment
Refuse the whole assignment for the shift
Ask the AP to watch the pump for alarms
questions.explanation: The PN raises the scope issue with the charge RN before the shift starts so the titration is reassigned to an RN while the PN keeps the rest of the care. Changing the rate at any time is outside the PN's role, and refusing the entire assignment is not necessary.

questions.stem: A resident on contact precautions for MRSA in a wound asks why the PN wears a gown and gloves but no mask. Which response is accurate?
options: "A mask is only needed when the wound is open."
"This germ spreads by touch, not through the air."
"The gown and gloves protect me from your coughing."
"I will put on a mask as well, to be safe."
questions.explanation: MRSA in a wound spreads by direct and indirect contact, so a gown and gloves block transmission and a mask adds nothing. A mask would be added only for a procedure likely to splash or if the organism were in the sputum.

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia tells the PN, "The TV is sending me messages to leave." Which response is best?
options: "The TV cannot send anyone any messages at all."
"What do you think the messages mean?"
"Let's turn the TV off so it stops."
"I don't get messages from the TV, but that sounds frightening."
questions.explanation: The PN presents reality without arguing and acknowledges the feeling behind the delusion. Flatly contradicting the client provokes defensiveness, exploring the content reinforces the delusion, and turning off the TV implies the messages are real.

questions.stem: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM is prescribed. After reconstitution the vial contains 350 mg per mL. How many mL should the PN draw up? Record your answer to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: 500 mg divided by 350 mg/mL is 1.43 mL, which rounds to 1.4 mL. Dividing the other way gives 0.7 mL, which would deliver only half the dose.

questions.stem: A client who takes lithium has a morning level of 0.8 mEq/L and no new symptoms. Which action should the PN take?
options: Hold the dose and notify the RN
Encourage the client to limit fluids
Give a double dose to raise the level
Give the dose as scheduled
questions.explanation: A lithium level of 0.8 mEq/L is within the usual maintenance range of about 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L, so the dose is given. Fluids are kept steady, not limited, because dehydration raises the level, and only the provider changes a dose.

questions.stem: A parent tells the PN that a 2-year-old eats "almost nothing" at dinner. Which response is appropriate?
options: "Offer a sweet dessert as a reward for eating."
"Appetite drops as growth slows in toddlers."
"Give a large glass of milk with each meal."
"Have the child sit until the plate is finished."
questions.explanation: Growth slows after the first year, so toddlers eat less and in bursts, and small servings with healthy snacks meet their needs. Food rewards, forced sitting and large amounts of milk that replace food all create poor eating habits.

questions.stem: The PN transfers a client with right-sided weakness from the bed to a wheelchair placed on the client's left side. Place the steps in the order the PN should perform them.
options: Lock the wheelchair brakes
Help the client sit on the edge of the bed
Fasten the gait belt around the client's waist
Stand the client up on a count of three
Pivot the client toward the chair on the stronger leg
Lower the client into the seat
questions.explanation: The chair is locked before the client moves, the client sits and dangles so dizziness shows up while still on the bed, the gait belt goes on before standing, and the client stands, pivots on the strong left leg toward the chair on that side, and is lowered into the seat. A belt fastened after standing or an unlocked chair is where falls happen.

questions.stem: At a clinic, a caller who says he is a client's employer asks the PN whether the client was seen today. What should the PN do?
options: Confirm the visit but not the reason
Transfer the call to the provider
Decline to share any information
Ask the employer to put the request in writing
questions.explanation: Even confirming that someone is a client is protected health information and cannot be released without the client's written authorization. The provider has the same limits, and a written request from the employer does not replace the client's permission.

questions.stem: A client on a medical unit reports chest pressure that spreads to the jaw and has not eased with 10 minutes of rest. Which action should the PN take first?
options: Stay with the client and call the RN
Help the client walk to relieve the pressure
Give an antacid from the stock supply
Document the report and recheck in 30 minutes
questions.explanation: Chest pressure spreading to the jaw and unrelieved by rest may be a heart attack, so the PN stays with the client, keeps the client at rest and gets the RN so oxygen, an ECG and medications can be started. Walking increases the heart's work, and an antacid or a 30-minute wait delays treatment.

questions.stem: While wiping a counter, the PN splashes a cleaning solution into one eye. What should the PN do first?
options: Read the safety data sheet for the chemical
Report the exposure to the supervisor
Flush the eye with water for 15 minutes
Apply an ophthalmic ointment to the eye
questions.explanation: Immediate flushing with water limits chemical damage to the eye, which is why eyewash stations are in work areas. The safety data sheet and the report to the supervisor follow the flushing, and ointment is not applied to a chemical exposure.

questions.stem: Before assigning the AP to walk a resident in the hall, which question is most important for the PN to answer?
options: Does the AP want to do the task?
Will the task take more than 10 minutes?
Has the AP walked other residents today?
Is the resident's condition stable?
questions.explanation: A task is assigned only when the resident's condition is stable and the outcome predictable, which is the right circumstance for delegation. The AP's preference and the time the task takes do not decide whether it is safe to assign.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old with anorexia nervosa is admitted to a medical unit. Which action by the PN is appropriate at mealtimes?
options: Sit with the client during the meal
Let the client eat alone to reduce stress
Discuss calorie counts while the client eats
Allow bathroom use right after the meal
questions.explanation: Staying with the client during and for a period after meals supports eating and prevents hiding food or purging. Eating alone and unsupervised bathroom trips allow the behaviors to continue, and talking about calories raises anxiety.

questions.stem: A child who weighs 18 kg is prescribed acetaminophen 15 mg/kg PO. The oral liquid is labeled 160 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the PN give? Record your answer to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: 15 mg/kg times 18 kg is 270 mg. 160 mg per 5 mL is 32 mg per mL, and 270 mg divided by 32 mg/mL is 8.44 mL, which rounds to 8.4 mL. Forgetting to multiply by the weight gives 0.5 mL, far below the dose.

questions.stem: The PN helps care for a client with a chest tube connected to a water-seal drainage system. Which findings should the PN report to the RN? Select all that apply.
options: Continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber
The water level in the water seal rises and falls with breathing
New crackling felt under the skin around the insertion site
300 mL of bright red drainage in the last hour
The drainage system is positioned below the chest
questions.explanation: Constant bubbling in the water seal means an air leak, crepitus around the site means air is escaping into the tissue, and 300 mL of bright red blood in an hour is active bleeding. Tidaling with breathing and a system kept below the chest are what is expected.

questions.stem: The PN is collecting data from a 15-year-old at a sports physical. The parent is in the room. Which action is appropriate?
options: Direct all of the questions to the parent
Skip the questions about sexual activity
Interview the teen alone for part of it
Have the parent answer about substance use
questions.explanation: Adolescents give honest answers about mood, substances and sexual activity when they are interviewed privately, so part of the visit is done without the parent. Skipping those questions or routing them through the parent misses the main health risks of this age group.

questions.stem: The PN feeds a client who has dysphagia after a stroke. Which action is correct?
options: Offer thin liquids through a straw between bites
Sit the client upright with the chin tucked
Place each bite of food on the weak side of the mouth
Feed quickly so the client does not become tired
questions.explanation: An upright position with a slight chin tuck narrows the airway entrance and makes swallowing safer. Thin liquids and straws are the easiest things to aspirate, food goes on the strong side of the mouth, and feeding is slow with a check that each bite is swallowed.

questions.stem: The PN gives a client's 0900 medications 2 hours late. The client is unharmed. What should the PN do?
options: Notify the RN and file an incident report
Document the medications as given at 0900
Tell the client not to mention the delay
Skip the next dose to avoid an overlap
questions.explanation: A late dose is a medication error even when no harm results, so the PN reports it to the RN and completes an incident report so the cause can be found. Charting the wrong time or hiding the delay falsifies the record, and skipping the next dose is a second error.

questions.stem: The PN notices that a client's personal electric razor has a frayed cord. What should the PN do?
options: Wrap the frayed area with tape
Allow its use only when the PN is present
Ask the family to take it home at the next visit
Take the razor out of use and report it
questions.explanation: A frayed cord can shock the client or start a fire, so the device is removed from use at once and reported so it can be checked or replaced. Tape, supervision and waiting for a visit all leave the hazard in the room.

questions.stem: A client with advanced cancer tells the PN, "I want to stop the chemotherapy, but my son will be angry." Which response is appropriate?
options: "Your son only wants what's best for you."
"Tell me more about what you want."
"You should finish the course your doctor ordered."
"Let me call your son so you can talk."
questions.explanation: An open question lets the client explore the decision, which belongs to the client alone. Siding with the son or the provider pressures the client, and calling the son shifts the focus away from the client's own wishes.

questions.stem: A client receiving hospice care says to the PN, "I'm ready to go, but my family keeps telling me to fight." Which response is therapeutic?
options: "Your family just wants more time with you."
"Tell me more about feeling ready."
"You should keep fighting for your family."
"Would you like me to call the chaplain now?"
questions.explanation: An open invitation lets the client talk about acceptance and the strain with the family. Speaking for the family, urging the client to fight or handing the conversation to someone else all stop the client from being heard.

questions.stem: An older adult is being treated for pneumonia. Which finding shows the PN that the client is improving?
options: Respirations 28/min
SpO2 95% on room air
Coughing up rust-colored sputum
Temperature 101 F
questions.explanation: A saturation of 95% without oxygen means the lungs are exchanging gas well again. Fast breathing, fever and rust-colored sputum are signs the infection is still active.

questions.stem: The PN gives enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe to a client after hip surgery. Which action is correct?
options: Massage the site for a minute after the injection
Pull back on the plunger before injecting the drug
Inject into the deltoid muscle of the nondominant arm
Leave the air bubble in the syringe when injecting
questions.explanation: The small air bubble in a prefilled enoxaparin syringe is left in so the full dose is delivered and the drug does not leak back along the track. It is given subcutaneously in the abdomen, without aspirating or massaging, because both increase bruising.

questions.stem: A clinic client with type 2 diabetes has a hemoglobin A1c of 9.2%. The PN understands that this result shows which of the following?
options: Blood glucose has averaged high over the last 2 to 3 months
Blood glucose was high only at the time the blood was drawn
Blood glucose control has been at the usual goal for most adults
The client had a recent episode of hypoglycemia that needs follow-up
questions.explanation: The A1c reflects average glucose over the life of the red blood cell, about 2 to 3 months, and the usual goal for most adults is below 7%. A single fasting glucose shows one moment, which an A1c does not.

questions.stem: A client's living will refuses intubation. The client's daughter tells the PN that she wants "everything done" if her mother stops breathing. What should the PN do?
options: Tell the daughter the living will cannot be changed
Ask the daughter to sign a new consent form
Notify the RN of the daughter's request
Remove the living will from the chart
questions.explanation: A conflict between a family member and a client's advance directive is reported to the RN so the provider, the client if able and the family can meet. The client's documented wishes stand unless the client changes them; a family member cannot sign them away.

questions.stem: A client at 32 weeks of pregnancy calls the clinic. Which report should the PN tell the RN about immediately?
options: Swollen feet at the end of the day
Heartburn after large meals
Leg cramps at night
Blurred vision and a headache
questions.explanation: Headache with visual changes in the third trimester is a warning sign of preeclampsia and needs evaluation the same day. Ankle swelling by evening, heartburn and leg cramps are common discomforts of late pregnancy.

questions.stem: A client has been on bed rest for 3 days after a fall. Which measures should the PN use to prevent complications of immobility? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage use of the incentive spirometer
Keep a pillow under the knees at all times
Perform range-of-motion exercises
Reposition at least every 2 hours
Restrict fluids to reduce voiding
questions.explanation: Deep breathing, range of motion and regular turning protect the lungs, joints, skin and circulation of a client on bed rest. A pillow kept under the knees slows venous return and promotes clots and contractures, and restricting fluids thickens secretions and concentrates urine.

questions.stem: A client in bed begins having a tonic-clonic seizure. Which action should the PN take?
options: Turn the client onto the side
Hold the client's arms still
Place a padded tongue blade in the mouth
Move the client to the floor
questions.explanation: Turning the client to the side lets saliva drain and keeps the airway open while the PN protects the head and times the seizure. Nothing goes in the mouth, the limbs are never held, and a client already in bed is kept there with the rails padded.

questions.stem: A client on a medical unit is shouting, clenching his fists and pacing near the door. What should the PN do first?
options: Block the doorway so the client stays in the room
Tell the client to sit down right now
Stay out of reach and speak calmly
Touch the client's arm to reassure him
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance, a calm voice and an open path to the door protects the PN and gives the client room to settle while help is called. Blocking the exit, commands and touch all feel threatening and can trigger an assault.

questions.stem: The RN asks the PN to help admit a stable client transferred from another unit. Which part of the admission is within the PN's role?
options: Completing the comprehensive admission assessment
Developing the initial plan of care
Deciding which nursing problems take priority
Collecting vital signs and health history data
questions.explanation: The PN collects data such as vital signs, weight, allergies and history, and contributes it to the plan. The comprehensive assessment, the initial plan of care and setting priorities are the RN's responsibilities.

questions.stem: A client is starting levothyroxine for hypothyroidism. Which instruction should the PN reinforce?
options: Take it on an empty stomach in the morning
Take it with breakfast to prevent stomach upset
Take it at bedtime with a glass of milk
Take it only on days you feel tired
questions.explanation: Levothyroxine is absorbed best on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast and apart from calcium, iron and antacids. It is a lifelong daily medication, and food, milk or dairy reduce how much is absorbed.

questions.stem: A client's sodium level is 128 mEq/L. Which findings should the PN watch for?
options: Thirst and dry, sticky mucous membranes
Confusion and headache
Tall, peaked T waves
Twitching of the face when the cheek is tapped
questions.explanation: Low sodium pulls water into brain cells, so headache, confusion, nausea and, if severe, seizures are the signs to watch. Thirst and dry membranes go with high sodium, peaked T waves with high potassium, and facial twitching with low calcium.

questions.stem: The PN is reinforcing teaching with a client who uses home oxygen. Which statement by the client shows a need for further teaching?
options: "I post no-smoking signs on my doors."
"I keep the tank by the stove while I cook."
"I use water-based lotion on my face."
"I keep the tubing away from the space heater."
questions.explanation: Oxygen feeds a fire, so the tank and tubing stay at least 10 feet from stoves, heaters and open flames. No-smoking signs, water-based lotion instead of petroleum products and distance from heaters are correct practices.

questions.stem: The PN is assigned four clients on a medical unit. Which client should the PN check first?
options: Client on oxygen whose SpO2 alarm is sounding
Client requesting a pain medication that is due
Client whose IV bag has 50 mL remaining
Client asking to speak with the dietitian
questions.explanation: An oxygen saturation alarm may mean a client is not breathing adequately, which comes before pain, an IV bag that is nearly empty or a dietitian request. The PN checks the client, not just the monitor, and reports a low reading to the RN.

questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis is admitted to a medical unit. Which finding should the PN report to the RN as a sign of bleeding?
options: Yellow color of the sclera
An enlarged, rounded abdomen
Black, tarry stools
Spider-shaped veins on the chest
questions.explanation: Black, tarry stools mean digested blood from the upper gastrointestinal tract, often from varices, and are reported at once. Jaundice, ascites and spider angiomas are chronic signs of liver disease rather than active bleeding.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old client asks the PN how to cope with hot flashes during menopause. Which suggestion is appropriate?
options: Dress in layers and keep the room cool
Drink a cup of hot tea before bedtime
Skip exercise until the hot flashes stop
Have a glass of wine in the evening
questions.explanation: Layers that can be removed, a cool room and avoiding triggers reduce the discomfort of hot flashes. Hot drinks, alcohol and inactivity make them worse.

questions.stem: The PN cares for a client with an indwelling urinary catheter. Which action is correct?
options: Disconnect the tubing to collect a urine specimen
Rest the drainage bag on the floor during transfers
Keep the drainage bag below the level of the bladder
Clamp the catheter for 2 hours every shift to train the bladder
questions.explanation: The bag stays below the bladder and off the floor so urine drains freely and does not flow back toward the bladder. Specimens come from the sampling port with the system kept closed, and routine clamping holds urine in the bladder and raises infection risk.

questions.stem: A client asks the PN to pray with him before surgery. The PN does not share the client's faith. Which response is appropriate?
options: Explain that the PN cannot pray with clients
Suggest the client wait for the chaplain
Pretend to share the client's beliefs
Stay with the client while he prays
questions.explanation: Being present while the client prays meets the spiritual need without the PN having to share the belief, and a chaplain can be offered in addition. Refusing or deferring leaves the client without support before surgery, and pretending is dishonest.

questions.stem: The PN has 30 minutes left in the shift and four tasks remaining. Which task should the PN complete first?
options: Restock the linen cart in the supply hallway
Give an antibiotic due 20 minutes ago
Document a routine dressing change
Return a family member's phone call
questions.explanation: A late antibiotic affects the client's treatment, so it comes before documentation, restocking and a non-urgent phone call. The dressing change should still be charted before the shift ends.

questions.passage: 1130 Nurses' note: {{Skin cool and sweaty}}. {{Hands shaking}}. {{Asks what time lunch is three times in 5 minutes}}. {{BP 138/82 mm Hg}}. {{Heart rate 104/min}}. {{Lungs clear in all fields}}. {{Says, "I feel funny and weak."}}
questions.stem: The PN compares these findings with the resident's baseline. Highlight the findings that require follow-up.
questions.explanation: Sweating, tremor, a fast pulse, weakness and new repetitive questioning in a resident who is usually oriented and conversational are the early signs of low blood sugar after a sulfonylurea with little breakfast. The blood pressure is near her usual range and clear lungs are reassuring.

questions.passage: 1135: Capillary glucose 48 mg/dL. The 0800 glipizide dose was given, and insulin glargine 20 units was given at 2100 last night.
questions.stem: For each finding, specify whether it supports hypoglycemia or does not point to hypoglycemia.
questions.explanation: Sweating, a fast pulse and tremor come from the adrenaline released when glucose falls, and confusion comes from the brain running short of glucose. Her blood pressure is close to her usual and clear lungs do not point to hypoglycemia one way or the other.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence. The resident is most likely experiencing [[1]] caused by [[2]], and the greatest immediate risk is [[3]].
blanks: loss of consciousness and a fall
questions.explanation: A glucose of 48 mg/dL with sweating, tremor and confusion is hypoglycemia, and the cause is a full dose of a sulfonylurea taken with only a quarter of breakfast, on top of her usual basal insulin. Untreated, she can become unconscious, seize or fall; ketoacidosis is a high-glucose problem and her pressure is near her usual.

questions.passage: 1135: Capillary glucose 48 mg/dL. The resident is awake, answers to her name and swallows a sip of water without coughing.
